tree/tertullian-s-voice.quote: Rival teachers used the Scriptures too, for teachings the churches rejected.
tree/tertullian-s-voice.asks: What did Marcion and Valentinus teach?

tree/tertullian-s-voice.quote: later he broke from the prophets too and gathered meetings of his own
tree/tertullian-s-voice.asks: Why did he break from the prophets, and over what?

tree/tertullian-s-voice.quote: the very few who were left crossed into the Catholic church, the main body, and handed over their church building

f.quote: If they could not look into the charges openly, from the judge's seat
Jerome, who wrote his life, says the envy and insults of the clergy of Rome drove him to it.
f.asks: Why did the Roman clergy envy and insult him?

f.quote: Valentinus kept them whole but bent their meaning

hearts.tree/tertullian-s-voice: Tertullian of Carthage, the first great Christian writer in Latin, defended Christians to Rome's governors, claimed the Scriptures for the apostles' churches, and gave Latin its words for God as one and three. Later he joined the strict New Prophecy and turned against the bishops, yet the Latin church kept reading him.
